page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc6.8xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 16 physical Intel Xeon 8269CY cores running at a base clock speed of 3.1 GHz. The x86_64 architecture supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and AVX512_VNNI, which accelerate vector and neural network operations. The instance is configured with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 2.0 GB memory-to-vCPU ratio. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 10 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the ecs.hfc6.8xlarge demonstrates solid compute and memory performance. The Intel Xeon processor achieves a single-core stress-ng score of 1435.39 and a multi-core score of 30631.79, alongside a Geekbench multi-core score of 10887.0. Memory bandwidth tests show cached read speeds of 1704.01 GB/sec and uncached large-block write speeds of 36.58 GB/sec. For specialized workloads, the instance processes 29.05 million Redis SET operations per second and delivers a static web serving throughput of 20.59 GB/sec. It also handles small-scale LLM inference, processing 46.11 prompt tokens per second on a medium 7B model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.hfc6.8xlarge offers a high-density compute profile with dedicated CPU allocation, making it a viable option for CPU-bound tasks that do not require massive memory footprints. However, the 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU represents a tradeoff for memory-intensive applications, and the lack of local NVMe storage requires reliance on network storage, which may impact I/O-heavy operations. This instance is well-suited for workloads such as software compilation, web serving, high-throughput database operations, and moderate parallel processing tasks.
